idiom_name: memberwise/labeled initializer with argument labels and default values
implementation_notes: Swift's initializers already give the two guarantees a staged builder adds: every stored property must be initialized before the instance is usable (the compiler rejects a partial init) and arguments are labeled and checked in order, so a struct with a memberwise initializer and default values is the local replacement for the staged chain. The staged form is written with one small type (or protocol) per step when the sequence itself is the invariant or when a step performs side effects - connecting, opening a file, acquiring a lock. Keep the classic structure for APIs consumed from Objective-C or when the intermediate stages must be resumable; in Swift the staged types are usually structs whose transitions return the next stage value.
pitfalls: The implicit memberwise initializer of a public struct is internal, so a library API must declare its initializers explicitly or callers in another module cannot construct the type at all.
Class initializers run in two phases and can leave properties temporarily unset; when a step can fail, use a failable/throwing initializer or a staged type instead of mutating a half-built instance.

Staged builders as structs copy their state on every transition, so large payloads are copied per step; make the transitions consuming (non-mutating methods returning the next stage) deliberately, and avoid holding an intermediate stage in a let and expecting it to advance.
